turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: I must say, Mr. Worthing, that your living arrangements are rather unconventional. A lady of my standing does not entertain those who are not firmly established in society.

turns.speaker: Gwendolen
turns.text: Mother, I do not think it is any of Mr. Worthing's concern to be firmly established in society. Surely, his character and intentions are what matter most.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Gwendolen, my dear, I must insist that in matters of marriage, one's social standing and stability are paramount. Mr. Worthing, you will forgive me, but your answers leave much to be desired.

turns.speaker: Gwendolen
turns.text: Mother, you are being excessively strict. Mr. Worthing's intentions and character are evident, and they should speak for themselves.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Gwendolen, I appreciate your enthusiasm, but I must maintain a certain standard. Mr. Worthing, I suggest you consider the importance of a stable and respectable background.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: I understand your concerns, Lady Bracknell, and I assure you that my intentions are honourable. I am eager to provide the stability that you and Gwendolen deserve.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Mr. Worthing, while your assurances are noted, I require concrete evidence of your stability and social position. Your character is indeed important, but it must be supported by a respectable background.

turns.speaker: Gwendolen
turns.text: Mother, you are being unreasonable. Mr. Worthing's character is more important than his background, and I will not be swayed.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Gwendolen, your eagerness to overlook the importance of a respectable background is troubling. Mr. Worthing, I am not questioning your character, but the stability of your circumstances is of utmost importance.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: I understand your concerns, Lady Bracknell, and I will do everything in my power to provide the stability you seek. I respect your standards and wish to meet them.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Mr. Worthing, I appreciate your commitment. However, I must insist on a detailed account of your financial status and family connections before I can entertain the idea of your marriage to Gwendolen. Your character is indeed commendable, but it is the foundation of your social standing that I am concerned with.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Lady Bracknell, I understand your need for transparency and I will provide all the information you require to your satisfaction. My intention is to ensure Gwendolen's happiness and security.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Mr. Worthing, I appreciate your earnestness. However, until I am fully satisfied with your financial stability and family connections, I cannot consider the possibility of your marriage to Gwendolen. Your intentions are commendable, but actions speak louder than words.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: I will provide you with all the information you require, Lady Bracknell. I wish to meet your expectations and ensure Gwendolen's happiness.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Mr. Worthing, I shall expect a comprehensive report on your finances and background at my earliest convenience. Until then, I cannot proceed with any further discussion of this matter.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: I shall prepare the information you require, Lady Bracknell, and bring it to you at your earliest convenience.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: I trust you will be prompt and precise in your documentation, Mr. Worthing. Gwendolen's future is not to be trifled with.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Yes, Lady Bracknell, I understand the importance of this matter. I shall work diligently to provide you with the details you need.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: I trust, Mr. Worthing, that you are aware of the importance of adhering to our society's conventions. Any deviation could jeopardize my daughter's prospects.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: I understand perfectly, Lady Bracknell. I assure you that I will adhere strictly to all societal conventions and do everything in my power to ensure Gwendolen's future is secure.

opening.speaker: Gwendolen
opening.text: I am engaged to Mr. Worthing, mamma.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Pardon me, you are not engaged to any one. When you do become engaged to some one, I, or your father, will inform you of the fact. An engagement should come on a young girl as a surprise, pleasant or unpleasant, as the case may be. It is hardly a matter that she could be allowed to arrange for herself . . . And now I have a few questions to put to you, Mr. Worthing. While I am making these inquiries, you, Gwendolen, will wait for me below in the carriage.

opening.speaker: Gwendolen
opening.text: Mamma!

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: In the carriage, Gwendolen!

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Gwendolen, the carriage!

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: You can take a seat, Mr. Worthing.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Thank you, Lady Bracknell, I prefer standing.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: I feel bound to tell you that you are not down on my list of eligible young men, although I have the same list as the dear Duchess of Bolton has. We work together, in fact. However, I am quite ready to enter your name, should your answers be what a really affectionate mother requires. Do you smoke?

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Well, yes, I must admit I smoke.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: I am glad to hear it. A man should always have an occupation of some kind. There are far too many idle men in London as it is. How old are you?

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Twenty-nine.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: A very good age to be married at. I have always been of opinion that a man who desires to get married should know either everything or nothing. Which do you know?

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: I know nothing, Lady Bracknell.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: I am pleased to hear it. I do not approve of anything that tampers with natural ignorance. Ignorance is like a delicate exotic fruit; touch it and the bloom is gone. The whole theory of modern education is radically unsound. Fortunately in England, at any rate, education produces no effect whatsoever. If it did, it would prove a serious danger to the upper classes, and probably lead to acts of violence in Grosvenor Square. What is your income?

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Between seven and eight thousand a year.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: In land, or in investments?

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: In investments, chiefly.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: That is satisfactory. What between the duties expected of one during one’s lifetime, and the duties exacted from one after one’s death, land has ceased to be either a profit or a pleasure. It gives one position, and prevents one from keeping it up. That’s all that can be said about land.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: I have a country house with some land, of course, attached to it, about fifteen hundred acres, I believe; but I dons depend on that for my real income. In fact, as far as I can make out, the poachers are the only people who make anything out of it.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: A country house! How many bedrooms? Well, that point can be cleared up afterwards. You have a town house, I hope? A girl with a simple, unspoiled nature, like Gwendolen, could hardly be expected to reside in the country.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Well, I own a house in Belgrave Square, but it is let by the year to Lady Bloxham. Of course, I can get it back whenever I like, at six months’ notice.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bloxham? I don’t know her.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Oh, she goes about very little. She is a lady considerably advanced in years.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Ah, nowadays that is no guarantee of respectability of character. What number in Belgrave Square?
